context: seed: the world faults the leading HTTP calls of some tasks with a transient 502 (suite/tools.py:73), one or two calls per task (suite/faults.py:18), and every other error it raises is permanent; the genesis family and the faulted arms of probe and transfer meet it
counterfactual: The overshoot is retrying every failure — the 410 of a moved route, the 401 of a secure route — as if transient, a retry storm bounded by suite/tools.py:73 (the one transient fault the world raises) against suite/tools.py:75 (a 404 that names no fix); the other overshoot is stopping at the first 502 when suite/faults.py:18 faults two leading calls.
decision: A tool failure whose cause is marked transient (`HTTP 502 Bad Gateway from <path> (transient)`) is retried on the same path: the world faults at most the first two calls of a task, so retry up to twice, then report. Any other status — 401, 404, 410, a budget refusal — is never retried: each names its own fix (the token, the /v2 successor) or none, and a retry repeats it. An error that is reported carries the underlying cause verbatim.

residue: whether two retries is the right bound is the fault profile's number; a profile that faults more calls moves it

not_this: a 4xx or a budget refusal, which a retry cannot repair — a 401, 404 or 410 names its own fix or none
a failure inside the model's own reasoning, with no tool call behind it

lifecycle.consumer: the working pass, at boot, on a matching work-shape
lifecycle.moot_when: the fault profile faults no HTTP call

options.name: A — retry a transient 502 on the same path, up to twice; report anything else with its cause
options.why: clears the world's faults within their bound and keeps the budget for the answer

options.name: B — retry every failure
options.why: a 410 or 401 repeats on every retry; the budget goes and the error names a fix the retry ignores

options.name: C — report the first failure
options.why: the transient fault clears on the next call and the row was one call from passing

summary.latch: an HTTP call that fails with a 502 marked transient; an error to be reported from a tool failure
not_this: a 4xx or a budget refusal, which a retry cannot repair — a 401, 404 or 410 names its own fix or none
a failure inside the model's own reasoning, with no tool call behind it
summary.stakes: a task that stops at a transient fault scores zero when the next call would answer; a retry on a permanent status spends the budget and repeats the failure

premises.falsifier: a third consecutive 502 on the same path
premises.statement: the transient fault clears within the faulted leading calls

premises.falsifier: a 502 whose cause lacks the transient mark
premises.statement: the tool marks a transient failure as such in the cause
